RHEL9 ELK Stack Upgrade - Complete Guide

RHEL9 ELK Stack Upgrade - Complete Guide

Document Version: 2.0 | Date: 2026-07-10
Purpose: Comprehensive guide for RHEL9 ELK Stack migration via cluster expansion
Strategy: Gradual cluster node replacement (RHEL8 nodes add RHEL9 nodes → Remove RHEL8 → All RHEL9)

Table of Contents

  1. Migration Strategy

  2. Quick Reference.

  3. System Architecture - Before & After

  4. Pre-Migration Preparation

  5. Elasticsearch Migration (Core)

  6. Logstash Migration

  7. Kibana Migration

  8. Fleet & Beats Migration

  9. Post-Migration Validation

  10. Troubleshooting & Emergency

0. Migration Strategy

This is a GRADUAL NODE REPLACEMENT strategy within the SAME cluster:

EXISTING CLUSTER STAYS ONLINE THE WHOLE TIME │ ├─ PHASE 1: Add RHEL9 Nodes │ ├─ Keep existing RHEL8 cluster running (9-10 nodes) │ ├─ Provision new RHEL9 servers with same roles │ ├─ Configure new RHEL9 nodes to JOIN existing cluster │ ├─ Monitor as RHEL9 nodes join and balance │ └─ Result: 18-20 nodes total (9-10 RHEL8 + 9-10 RHEL9) │ ├─ PHASE 2: Rebalance Data to RHEL9 Nodes │ ├─ Let Elasticsearch redistribute shards to RHEL9 nodes │ ├─ Data flows to new nodes automatically │ ├─ Monitor shard movement │ └─ Result: Data balanced across all nodes (old + new) │ └─ PHASE 3: Remove RHEL8 Nodes One-by-One ├─ Cordon RHEL8 node (no new shards) ├─ Wait for shards to migrate to RHEL9 nodes ├─ Stop service and remove from cluster ├─ Repeat for each RHEL8 node └─ Result: Cluster with only RHEL9 nodes (same size) TIMELINE: Test Environment: 8 RHEL8 nodes → 8-10 RHEL8+RHEL9 → 8-10 RHEL9 nodes Prod Environment: 19 RHEL8 nodes → 19+19 RHEL8+RHEL9 → 19 RHEL9 nodes

Key Differences from Full Cluster Replacement:

Aspect

Old Approach (Full Replacement)

New Approach (Gradual Expansion)

Aspect

Old Approach (Full Replacement)

New Approach (Gradual Expansion)

Cluster Name

New cluster created

SAME cluster the whole time

Master Quorum

Need 3 new masters, old cluster separate

Add 3 RHEL9 masters, they join existing quorum

Data

Snapshot → restore to new cluster

Auto-rebalance to new nodes (no snapshot)

Services

Point to new cluster after cutover

No service endpoint changes needed

Downtime

Minimal but requires cutover window

Zero downtime (rolling node replacement)

Complexity

Higher (manage two clusters)

Lower (manage one growing/shrinking cluster)

Speed

Faster (parallel deployment)

Slower (sequential node replacement)

Migration Phases (Cluster Expansion Approach)

Phase 1: Prepare & Add RHEL9 Nodes to Cluster

  • Provision new RHEL9 servers with same roles as current RHEL8

  • Deploy Elasticsearch 8.18.1 on new RHEL9 nodes

  • Configure new nodes to discover and join the EXISTING cluster

  • Result: Cluster temporarily has both RHEL8 + RHEL9 nodes

Phase 2: Rebalance Data & Validate

  • Elasticsearch automatically rebalances shards to new RHEL9 nodes

  • Verify all nodes healthy and communicating

  • Confirm data balanced evenly across all nodes

  • No downtime during this phase

Phase 3: Remove RHEL8 Nodes (Gradual)

  • One at a time, cordon RHEL8 node (disable new shards)

  • Wait for shards to migrate to RHEL9 nodes

  • Stop Elasticsearch and remove from cluster

  • Repeat until all RHEL8 nodes removed

  • Result: Cluster contains only RHEL9 nodes (same size as original)

Phase 4: Validation & Decommission

  • Final health checks

  • Archive old RHEL8 servers

  • Deactivate old credentials/certificates

1. Master Node Handling

Summary: RHEL9 master nodes are added to the existing Elasticsearch cluster through the standard Ansible deployment. They join the current master quorum automatically, and Elasticsearch manages leader election without a separate cutover process.

Because this migration keeps the same cluster online throughout the upgrade, supporting services continue using the existing Elasticsearch endpoints while the cluster expands and contracts.

Component

What Happens

Component

What Happens

Masters

Deploy RHEL9, join existing cluster, election happens automatically

Data Nodes

Deploy RHEL9, join existing cluster, shards rebalance automatically

Logstash

Stays on old servers or deploy new, keeps pointing to same cluster

Kibana

Stays on old servers or deploy new, keeps pointing to same cluster

Fleet

Stays on old servers or deploy new, keeps pointing to same cluster

CLUSTER EXPANSION MIGRATION

Bottom Line: Add RHEL9 nodes to the existing cluster, let the cluster rebalance, then remove RHEL8 nodes. The cluster stays online throughout the migration.

Phase 1: Add RHEL9 Nodes (No Downtime)

OLD CLUSTER (9-10 nodes, RHEL8) ↓ (Add new servers, no deletions yet) EXPANDED CLUSTER (18-20 nodes, RHEL8 + RHEL9) ↓ (Elasticsearch auto-rebalances shards) BALANCED CLUSTER (18-20 nodes, data on both old + new)

Actions:

  1. Provision 9-10 new RHEL9 servers matching role distribution

  2. Run: ansible-playbook install_stack.yml -i inventories/elk-prod-rhel9.yml -e "join_existing_cluster=true"

  3. Monitor cluster → Should stay GREEN as RHEL9 nodes join

  4. Watch shards migrate to RHEL9 nodes automatically

  5. NO downtime, NO snapshot/restore, NO service changes

Phase 2: Remove RHEL8 Nodes One-by-One (Rolling Decommission)

BALANCED CLUSTER (18-20 nodes, mixed RHEL8 + RHEL9) ↓ (Cordon & drain RHEL8 node 1) CLUSTER (17-19 nodes + 1 cordoned) ↓ (Stop RHEL8 node 1) CLUSTER (17-19 nodes, one RHEL8 removed) ↓ (Repeat for each RHEL8 node) FINAL CLUSTER (9-10 nodes, all RHEL9)

Actions:

for each RHEL8_NODE: 1. Cordon: curl -X PUT https://MASTER:9200/_cluster/settings -d '{"transient": {"cluster.routing.allocation.exclude._name": "RHEL8_NODE"}}' 2. Wait: Monitor until all shards move to RHEL9 nodes (5-30 mins) 3. Stop: ssh RHEL8_NODE "sudo systemctl stop elasticsearch" 4. Remove: ssh RHEL8_NODE "sudo systemctl disable elasticsearch" 5. Verify: Cluster still GREEN, no data loss 6. Repeat for next RHEL8 node

Phase 3: Validation & Archive

  • Verify cluster is all RHEL9 nodes

  • Confirm no data loss, all indices present

  • Archive old RHEL8 servers (can keep for 7 days as safety)

  • Update documentation with new infrastructure

2. System Architecture - Before & After

Overview: Two Environments (Cluster Expansion Model)

  • TEST: Current RHEL8 cluster → Add RHEL9 nodes → Remove RHEL8 nodes → All RHEL9

  • PROD: Current production cluster → Add RHEL9 nodes → Remove RHEL8 nodes → All RHEL9

Key Point: Same cluster the whole time. No DNS changes, no service endpoint changes, no new Kibana/Logstash configuration needed.

TEST Environment: Cluster Expansion (RHEL8 → RHEL8+RHEL9 → RHEL9)

This is the working example. The same steps apply to production at larger scale.

TEST - PHASE 0 (Before Any Changes - Current RHEL8)

CURRENT RHEL8 CLUSTER (8-10 nodes): MASTER NODES (3): ├─ evelkmnn01.corp.fin [MASTER] - RHEL8 ├─ evelkmnn02.corp.fin [MASTER] - RHEL8 └─ evelkmnn03.corp.fin [MASTER] - RHEL8 DATA NODES (3-5): ├─ evelkwkn01.corp.fin [DATA_HOT, DATA_FROZEN, INGEST, ML] - RHEL8 ├─ evelkwkn02.corp.fin [DATA_HOT, DATA_WARM, DATA_COLD, DATA_FROZEN] - RHEL8 ├─ evelkwkn03.corp.fin [DATA_FROZEN] - RHEL8 └─ evelkinn01.corp.fin [INGEST] - RHEL8 KIBANA/LOGSTASH: ├─ evelkmnn01-03.corp.fin - RHEL8 (Kibana) ├─ evelkwkn01/02.corp.fin - RHEL8 (Logstash)

TEST - PHASE 1 (Cluster Expansion - RHEL8 + RHEL9)

ADD 8-10 NEW RHEL9 SERVERS (WITH SAME ROLES): MASTER NODES (6 total - 3 RHEL8 + 3 RHEL9): ├─ evelkmnn01.corp.fin [MASTER] - RHEL8 ├─ evelkmnn02.corp.fin [MASTER] - RHEL8 ├─ evelkmnn03.corp.fin [MASTER] - RHEL8 ├─ evelkmnn04.corp.fin [MASTER] - RHEL9 ← NEW ├─ evelkmnn05.corp.fin [MASTER] - RHEL9 ← NEW └─ evelkmnn06.corp.fin [MASTER] - RHEL9 ← NEW DATA NODES (6-10 total - mixed RHEL8 + RHEL9): ├─ evelkwkn01.corp.fin [DATA_HOT, DATA_FROZEN, INGEST, ML] - RHEL8 ├─ evelkwkn02.corp.fin [DATA_HOT, DATA_WARM, DATA_COLD, DATA_FROZEN] - RHEL8 ├─ evelkwkn03.corp.fin [DATA_FROZEN] - RHEL8 ├─ evelkinn01.corp.fin [INGEST] - RHEL8 ├─ evelkwkn04.corp.fin [DATA_HOT, DATA_FROZEN, INGEST, ML] - RHEL9 ← NEW ├─ evelkwkn05.corp.fin [DATA_HOT, DATA_WARM, DATA_COLD, DATA_FROZEN] - RHEL9 ← NEW ├─ evelkwkn06.corp.fin [DATA_FROZEN] - RHEL9 ← NEW STATUS: Cluster EXPANDED to ~16-18 nodes (still GREEN) Shards REBALANCING to new RHEL9 nodes Old RHEL8 nodes still have some data

TEST - PHASE 2 (Cluster Contraction - RHEL9 Only)

REMOVE RHEL8 NODES ONE-BY-ONE: After removing all 3-4 RHEL8 data nodes: ├─ evelkwkn04.corp.fin [DATA_HOT, DATA_FROZEN, INGEST, ML] - RHEL9 ├─ evelkwkn05.corp.fin [DATA_HOT, DATA_WARM, DATA_COLD, DATA_FROZEN] - RHEL9 ├─ evelkwkn06.corp.fin [DATA_FROZEN] - RHEL9 └─ evelkinn02.corp.fin [INGEST] - RHEL9 After removing all 3 RHEL8 masters: ├─ evelkmnn04.corp.fin [MASTER] - RHEL9 ├─ evelkmnn05.corp.fin [MASTER] - RHEL9 └─ evelkmnn06.corp.fin [MASTER] - RHEL9 FINAL STATE: 8-10 RHEL9 nodes (same size as original, but all new OS) Cluster name: UNCHANGED Endpoints: UNCHANGED Kibana/Logstash: UNCHANGED

Production Environment (Placeholder)

Actual production servers from inventories/elk-prod.yml:

PRODUCTION - PHASE 0 (Before - Current RHEL8 Only)

Current production cluster (existing):

PRODUCTION CLUSTER: "elasticsearch" MASTER NODES (3) ├─ evelkmnp01.corp.fin [MASTER] - RHEL8 ├─ evelkmnp02.corp.fin [MASTER] - RHEL8 └─ evelkmnp03.corp.fin [MASTER] - RHEL8 DATA NODES - HOT/WARM/COLD TIER (10 nodes) ├─ evelkwhp01-10.corp.fin [data_content, data_hot, data_warm, data_cold, ingest] - RHEL8 DATA NODES - FROZEN TIER (5 nodes) ├─ evelkwcp01-05.corp.fin [data_frozen] - RHEL8 MACHINE LEARNING (1 node) └─ evelkmlp01.corp.fin [ml] - RHEL8 TOTAL: 19 Elasticsearch nodes (all RHEL8) SUPPORTING SERVICES: ├─ Kibana: evelkkbp01-02 (RHEL8) ├─ Logstash: evelklsp01-12 (RHEL8) └─ Fleet: evelkftp01-02 (RHEL8)

PRODUCTION - PHASE 1 (Expansion - RHEL8 + RHEL9 Mixed)

After provisioning and adding new RHEL9 nodes (cluster expanded):

PRODUCTION CLUSTER: "elasticsearch" (SAME CLUSTER, EXPANDED) MASTER NODES (6 total - 3 old + 3 new) ├─ evelkmnp01.corp.fin [MASTER] - RHEL8 (original) ├─ evelkmnp02.corp.fin [MASTER] - RHEL8 (original) ├─ evelkmnp03.corp.fin [MASTER] - RHEL8 (original) ├─ [NEW_PROD_MASTER_1] [MASTER] - RHEL9 (newly joined) ├─ [NEW_PROD_MASTER_2] [MASTER] - RHEL9 (newly joined) └─ [NEW_PROD_MASTER_3] [MASTER] - RHEL9 (newly joined) DATA NODES - HOT TIER (20 total - mixed) ├─ evelkwhp01-10.corp.fin (RHEL8, rebalancing data out) └─ [NEW_PROD_HOT_1-10] (RHEL9, receiving data) DATA NODES - FROZEN TIER (10 total - mixed) ├─ evelkwcp01-05.corp.fin (RHEL8, rebalancing data out) └─ [NEW_PROD_FROZEN_1-5] (RHEL9, receiving data) MACHINE LEARNING (2 nodes) ├─ evelkmlp01.corp.fin (RHEL8) └─ [NEW_PROD_ML_1] (RHEL9) TOTAL: 38 Elasticsearch nodes (19 old RHEL8 + 19 new RHEL9) STATUS: Cluster GREEN, shards rebalancing to RHEL9 nodes SUPPORTING SERVICES (optional upgrade): ├─ Kibana: Still points to same cluster (no changes needed) ├─ Logstash: Still points to same cluster (no changes needed) └─ Fleet: Still points to same cluster (no changes needed)

PRODUCTION - PHASE 2 (Contraction - RHEL9 Only, Final State)

After removing all RHEL8 nodes one-by-one (cluster back to original size, all RHEL9):

PRODUCTION CLUSTER: "elasticsearch" (SAME CLUSTER, RHEL9 ONLY) MASTER NODES (3 - all RHEL9) ├─ [NEW_PROD_MASTER_1] [MASTER] - RHEL9 ├─ [NEW_PROD_MASTER_2] [MASTER] - RHEL9 └─ [NEW_PROD_MASTER_3] [MASTER] - RHEL9 DATA NODES - HOT TIER (10 - all RHEL9) ├─ [NEW_PROD_HOT_1-10] [data_content, data_hot, data_warm, data_cold, ingest] - RHEL9 DATA NODES - FROZEN TIER (5 - all RHEL9) ├─ [NEW_PROD_FROZEN_1-5] [data_frozen] - RHEL9 MACHINE LEARNING (1 - all RHEL9) └─ [NEW_PROD_ML_1] [ml] - RHEL9 TOTAL: 19 Elasticsearch nodes (all RHEL9, same as original) STATUS: Cluster GREEN, all data migrated, no RHEL8 nodes SUPPORTING SERVICES: ├─ Kibana: Still pointing to same cluster (no DNS/config changes) ├─ Logstash: Still pointing to same cluster (no config changes) └─ Fleet: Still pointing to same cluster (no endpoint changes) KEY POINT: Cluster name, endpoints, DNS - all UNCHANGED throughout migration

Migration Pre-Flight Validation Checklist

Before migration starts, verify all servers are accounted for:

ELASTICSEARCH CLUSTER ☐ All 3 master nodes documented (quorum required) ☐ All data nodes documented ☐ Frozen node documented (if applicable) ☐ Total nodes: ____ (expected 8-10) ☐ Each node has current IP, hostname, disk, memory ☐ Each node has new RHEL9 server assigned (1:1 mapping) KIBANA ☐ Both Kibana nodes documented ☐ Current DNS/LB configuration documented ☐ New Kibana IPs assigned ☐ DNS/LB update planned (date/time) LOGSTASH ☐ All 12 current Logstash servers documented ☐ New RHEL9 servers provisioned (14 total - capacity increase) ☐ Current load balancer backends documented ☐ LB update planned (date/time) FLEET ☐ All current Fleet servers documented ☐ New RHEL9 servers provisioned ☐ Enrollment tokens ready for agents CONNECTIVITY ☐ All current servers accessible via SSH ☐ All new servers accessible via SSH ☐ Network connectivity verified between old and new ☐ Firewall rules updated (if needed) CREDENTIALS ☐ Elasticsearch passwords ready ($ELASTICSEARCH_PASSWORD) ☐ Ansible vault passwords ready ☐ SSH keys ready for all servers ☐ TLS certificates generated for new servers BACKUP ☐ Pre-migration snapshot scheduled ☐ Snapshot location verified ☐ Retention policy documented ☐ Restore procedure tested

Pre-Flight Checklist (COMPLETE BEFORE MIGRATION STARTS)

System Requirements

#!/bin/bash echo "=== PRE-MIGRATION SYSTEM CHECK ===" # 1. Disk Space (50GB+ free minimum) echo "Disk Space Check:" for host in evelkmnp01 evelkmnp02 evelkmnp03 evelkwhp01 evelkwhp02 evelkwhp03 evelkinp01 evelkcfp01; do FREE=$(ssh $host.corp.fin df /var/lib/elasticsearch | awk 'NR==2 {print $4/1024/1024}') echo " $host: ${FREE}GB free" if (( $(echo "$FREE < 50" | bc -l) )); then echo " ❌ FAIL - Free space < 50GB" exit 1 fi done # 2. Network Connectivity echo "" echo "Network Connectivity:" for host in evelkmnp01 evelkmnp02 evelkmnp03; do ssh $host.corp.fin ping -c 1 evelkmnp02.corp.fin > /dev/null && echo " $host: ✅" || echo " $host: ❌" done # 3. Service Status echo "" echo "Service Status:" ansible elasticsearch -i inventories/elk-prod.yml -m service -a "name=elasticsearch state=started" --check # 4. Certificate Validity echo "" echo "Certificate Validity (remaining days):" for host in evelkmnp01 evelkmnp02 evelkmnp03; do ssh $host.corp.fin openssl x509 -in /etc/elasticsearch/certs/elasticsearch.crt -noout -checkend $((86400*30)) && echo " $host: ✅ Valid for >30 days" || echo " $host: ❌ Expiring soon" done

4. Elasticsearch Migration Using Ansible

4.0 Using Your Existing Repository

This repository contains the Ansible playbooks and roles needed for the RHEL9 migration:

  • Playbook: install_stack.yml deploys ELK Stack 8.18.1 to new servers

  • Inventory: Create inventories/elk-prod-rhel9.yml with new RHEL9 hostnames

  • Roles: Automatically configure Elasticsearch, Kibana, Logstash, and Fleet

  • Vault: Use group_vars/all/es_passwords.yml for secrets (encrypted)

4.1 Step 1: Create New RHEL9 Production Inventory (JOINING EXISTING CLUSTER)

IMPORTANT: The new RHEL9 nodes will JOIN the existing production cluster. They are NOT creating a new cluster.

Create inventories/elk-prod-rhel9.yml based on inventories/elk-prod.yml:

# inventories/elk-prod-rhel9.yml - Template for RHEL9 nodes joining existing cluster all: vars: elk_version: 8.18.1 certificate_name: "elasticsearch" # SAME as existing cluster group: elk env: prod es_cluster_name: "elasticsearch" # SAME as existing production cluster es_oidc_host: https://kibana.elk.omf.cloud # COPY vault-encrypted variables from elk-prod.yml children: elasticsearch: vars: # Copy ALL variables from elk-prod.yml elasticsearch section es_snapshot_cache_size: 5800gb snapshot_repositories: isilon: type: fs settings: location: /mnt/snapshots/prod # KEY: Use SAME cluster name so new nodes join existing cluster initial_bootstrap: false # Don't bootstrap a new cluster bootstrap_performed: true # These nodes are joining, not bootstrapping hosts: # Masters (3 NEW servers that will join existing master group) [NEW_PROD_MASTER_1]: # Maps to existing evelkmnp01 role es_node_roles: [ master ] [NEW_PROD_MASTER_2]: # Maps to existing evelkmnp02 role es_node_roles: [ master ] [NEW_PROD_MASTER_3]: # Maps to existing evelkmnp03 role es_node_roles: [ master ] # Hot/Warm/Cold Data (10 NEW servers) [NEW_PROD_HOT_1]: # Maps to evelkwhp01 role es_node_roles: [ data_content,data_hot,data_warm,data_cold,ingest,remote_cluster_client,transform ] [NEW_PROD_HOT_2]: es_node_roles: [ data_content,data_hot,data_warm,data_cold,ingest,remote_cluster_client,transform ] # ... continue through [NEW_PROD_HOT_10] # Frozen (5 NEW servers) [NEW_PROD_FROZEN_1]: # Maps to evelkwcp01 role es_node_roles: [ data_frozen ] # ... continue through [NEW_PROD_FROZEN_5] # ML (1 NEW server) [NEW_PROD_ML_1]: es_node_roles: [ ml ] kibana: # Copy from elk-prod.yml - they already work with the cluster hosts: [NEW_PROD_KIBANA_1]: # Optional: can also upgrade Kibana to RHEL9 [NEW_PROD_KIBANA_2]: # Optional: can also upgrade Kibana to RHEL9 logstash: # Copy from elk-prod.yml - they already work with the cluster hosts: [NEW_PROD_LOGSTASH_01]: logstash_heap_size: 64g # ... (01-12) Copy from existing fleet: # Copy from elk-prod.yml - they already work with the cluster hosts: [NEW_PROD_FLEET_1]: [NEW_PROD_FLEET_2]:

Key Differences from Full Cluster Replacement:

  • es_cluster_name: SAME as existing production cluster ("elasticsearch")

  • initial_bootstrap: FALSE (you're NOT creating a new cluster)

  • bootstrap_performed: TRUE (skip bootstrap logic)

  • Cluster discovery: New nodes will find existing cluster via DNS/seed hosts

  • Result: New RHEL9 nodes JOIN the existing cluster, increasing it to ~38 nodes temporarily

4.2 Step 2: Deploy New RHEL9 Nodes (Join Existing Cluster)

IMPORTANT: You're ADDING new RHEL9 nodes to the existing cluster, not creating a new cluster.

#!/bin/bash # Deploy new RHEL9 masters, data nodes, and supporting services # These nodes will join the existing "elasticsearch" cluster automatically ansible-playbook install_stack.yml \ -i inventories/elk-prod-rhel9.yml \ -e "install_serial=1" \ -e "initial_bootstrap=false" \ -e "bootstrap_performed=true" # This will: # 1. Deploy 3 new RHEL9 master nodes sequentially (serial:1 maintains quorum) # 2. Deploy 10 HOT/WARM/COLD data nodes # 3. Deploy 5 FROZEN tier data nodes # 4. Deploy 1 ML node # 5. (Optional) Deploy new Kibana/Logstash/Fleet on RHEL9 # 6. All new nodes join the existing "elasticsearch" cluster # 7. Elasticsearch auto-rebalances shards to new RHEL9 nodes

Expected Timeline:

  • Masters deployment: ~30 minutes (3 masters × 10 min each)

  • Data nodes deployment: ~60-90 minutes (15 data nodes × 5-6 min each)

  • Total: 90-120 minutes for all new nodes to join cluster

During Deployment, Monitor Cluster:

# In another terminal, monitor cluster expansion ENDPOINT="https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200" PASSWORD="$ELASTICSEARCH_PASSWORD" # Watch nodes join watch -n 10 'curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "$ENDPOINT/_cat/nodes?v" | head -30' # Watch shards rebalance watch -n 10 'curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "$ENDPOINT/_cat/shards?v" | grep RELO | wc -l' # Watch cluster health watch -n 10 'curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "$ENDPOINT/_cluster/health?pretty"'

4.2.5 What Happens When New Masters Join Existing Cluster

Key Facts About Master Election in Expanding Clusters:

  1. Existing Quorum (3 old RHEL8 masters) keeps cluster online

  2. New RHEL9 master 1 joins → 4 masters total (still 3-old in control)

  3. New RHEL9 master 2 joins → 5 masters total (still 3-old in control)

  4. New RHEL9 master 3 joins → 6 masters total (3-old + 3-new)

  5. After 30 seconds → Elasticsearch votes on new master quorum

  6. Usually elects from RHEL9 masters (same generation preference)

  7. Old RHEL8 masters still in cluster (waiting to be cordoned & removed)

No manual intervention needed - Elasticsearch handles this automatically.

Monitoring Master Transition:

#!/bin/bash ENDPOINT="https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200" PASSWORD="$ELASTICSEARCH_PASSWORD" echo "=== MONITORING MASTER TRANSITION ===" echo "" echo "Wait for this output to show new RHEL9 master as 'elected master':" echo "" for i in {1..60}; do echo "Iteration $i/60:" curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "$ENDPOINT/_cat/master" | head -1 echo "" sleep 5 done echo "" echo "✅ When you see a NEW RHEL9 hostname as 'elected master', transition complete"

4.2.6 Master Node Migration Checklist (Simplified for Cluster Expansion)

Phase 1: Add RHEL9 Masters to Existing Cluster (30 minutes)

Step 1: Run Ansible Deployment

ansible-playbook install_stack.yml \ -i inventories/elk-prod-rhel9.yml \ -e "install_serial=1" \ -e "initial_bootstrap=false"

Step 2: Wait for Node Discovery

# Check that new RHEL9 masters see the existing RHEL8 cluster ssh [NEW_PROD_MASTER_1] "curl -s http://localhost:9200/_cluster/health | jq '.cluster_name,.number_of_nodes'" # Expected Output: # "elasticsearch" # 6 (3 old RHEL8 + 3 new RHEL9)

Step 3: Verify Master Quorum

curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200/_cat/master # Should show either old master (still leading) or new master (took over) curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200/_cat/nodes | grep master # Should show 6 master-eligible nodes (3 RHEL8 + 3 RHEL9)

Step 4: Verify Cluster Health

curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200/_cluster/health | jq '{status, number_of_nodes, number_of_data_nodes, active_shards, unassigned_shards}' # Expected: # { # "status": "green", # "number_of_nodes": 6, # "number_of_data_nodes": 0, # "active_shards": XXX, # "unassigned_shards": 0 # }

Phase 2: Add RHEL9 Data Nodes to Cluster (60-90 minutes)

Step 5: Deploy Data Nodes

# Ansible continues deploying data nodes sequentially # Monitor rebalancing with: curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200/_cluster/health?pretty # "status" will be "yellow" or "green" as shards rebalance

Step 6: Wait for Rebalancing to Complete

#!/bin/bash ENDPOINT="https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200" PASSWORD="$ELASTICSEARCH_PASSWORD" echo "Waiting for shard rebalancing to complete..." echo "This can take 5-30 minutes depending on data volume" echo "" for i in {1..180}; do RELOCATING=$(curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "$ENDPOINT/_cat/shards" | grep RELO | wc -l) STATUS=$(curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "$ENDPOINT/_cluster/health" | jq -r '.status') NODES=$(curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "$ENDPOINT/_cat/nodes" | wc -l) echo "[$i/180] Status: $STATUS | Nodes: $NODES | Relocating: $RELOCATING shards" [ "$RELOCATING" -eq 0 ] && [ "$STATUS" = "green" ] && echo "✅ COMPLETE" && break sleep 10 done

Step 7: Verify All RHEL9 Nodes Joined

curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200/_cat/nodes?v # Should show: # - 3 old RHEL8 masters # - 3 new RHEL9 masters # - 10 old RHEL8 data nodes # - 10 new RHEL9 data nodes # - Etc. # Verify node count matches expected EXPECTED=38 # 19 old + 19 new ACTUAL=$(curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200/_cat/nodes | wc -l) echo "Nodes in cluster: $ACTUAL (expected $EXPECTED)"

Phase 3: Cordon & Remove RHEL8 Nodes (30 mins per node)

Step 8: For Each RHEL8 Node, Cordon It

#!/bin/bash # Do this for each RHEL8 node you want to remove RHEL8_NODE="evelkmnp01.corp.fin" # First master to remove ENDPOINT="https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200" PASSWORD="$ELASTICSEARCH_PASSWORD" echo "Cordoning $RHEL8_NODE..." # Prevent new shards from being assigned to this node curl -X PUT "$ENDPOINT/_cluster/settings" \ -u elastic:$PASSWORD \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d "{ \"transient\": { \"cluster.routing.allocation.exclude._name\": \"$RHEL8_NODE\" } }" # Monitor shard migration echo "Monitoring shard migration from $RHEL8_NODE..." for i in {1..120}; do SHARDS=$(curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "$ENDPOINT/_cat/shards" | grep "$RHEL8_NODE" | wc -l) echo "[$i/120] Shards on $RHEL8_NODE: $SHARDS" [ "$SHARDS" -eq 0 ] && echo "✅ All shards migrated" && break sleep 5 done

Step 9: Stop the RHEL8 Service

ssh root@evelkmnp01.corp.fin << 'EOF' echo "Stopping Elasticsearch..." systemctl stop elasticsearch systemctl disable elasticsearch echo "Verifying stopped..." sleep 5 systemctl status elasticsearch || echo "✅ Successfully stopped" EOF

Step 10: Remove Cordon & Verify Cluster Health

#!/bin/bash ENDPOINT="https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200" PASSWORD="$ELASTICSEARCH_PASSWORD" # Clear the exclusion to remove cordon curl -X PUT "$ENDPOINT/_cluster/settings" \ -u elastic:$PASSWORD \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "transient": { "cluster.routing.allocation.exclude._name": null } }' # Verify cluster still GREEN sleep 10 curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "$ENDPOINT/_cluster/health?pretty" | jq '{status, number_of_nodes, active_shards, unassigned_shards}'

Repeat Steps 8-10 for remaining RHEL8 nodes:

# Remove RHEL8 data nodes (evelkwhp01-10, evelkwcp01-05, evelkmlp01) # Then remove RHEL8 masters (evelkmnp02, evelkmnp03) # After all removed: # - Cluster has 19 RHEL9 nodes (same as original) # - Cluster name "elasticsearch" unchanged # - All Kibana/Logstash still working (no config changes needed) # - All endpoints unchanged

Phase 4: Verify Final State (30 mins)

Step 11: Verify 100% RHEL9

curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200/_cat/nodes?v | grep -i rhel # Should show all RHEL9, no RHEL8

Step 12: Archive Old RHEL8 Servers

# After 7-day monitoring confirms everything works: # - Power off old RHEL8 servers # - Remove from inventory # - Update documentation # - Remove DNS records (optional, can keep as historical)

Resolving [NEW_PROD_MASTER_1]...
Name: [NEW_PROD_MASTER_1]
Address: 10.1.1.50 ← NEW IP (not 10.1.1.10 which is old)

Resolving [NEW_PROD_MASTER_2]...
Name: [NEW_PROD_MASTER_2]
Address: 10.1.1.51 ← NEW IP

**If DNS is wrong:** Stop here and fix DNS before deploying. Bad DNS = clusters can't discover each other. #### 1.2 Verify Certificate Configuration ```bash #!/bin/bash # Verify certificate has Subject Alternative Names (SANs) for all new masters CERT_PATH="./temp/certificates/prod/[NEW_PROD_MASTER_1]_es.pem" echo "=== CERTIFICATE SAN CHECK ===" echo "Certificate must list all 3 new master hostnames" echo "" openssl x509 -in "$CERT_PATH" -text -noout | grep -A10 "Subject Alternative Name" echo "" echo "Required SANs:" echo " - [NEW_PROD_MASTER_1]" echo " - [NEW_PROD_MASTER_2]" echo " - [NEW_PROD_MASTER_3]" echo "" echo "If SANs are missing or wrong, get new certificate from Venafi BEFORE deploying"

If Certificate is Wrong:

# Request new cert with correct SANs from Venafi # This is org-specific - contact your security team

1.3 Backup Current Production Cluster State

#!/bin/bash echo "=== BACKING UP CURRENT CLUSTER STATE ===" PASSWORD="$ELASTICSEARCH_PASSWORD" BACKUP_DIR="/tmp/cluster-backups" mkdir -p "$BACKUP_DIR" # Get current cluster state from OLD production master echo "Backing up current cluster state..." curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD \ https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200/_cluster/state \ > "$BACKUP_DIR/cluster-state-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).json" # Get node info curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD \ https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200/_cat/nodes?v \ > "$BACKUP_DIR/nodes-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).txt" # Get shard allocation curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD \ https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200/_cat/shards?v \ > "$BACKUP_DIR/shards-before-migration.txt" # Document current state echo "" echo "✅ Backups saved to: $BACKUP_DIR" ls -la "$BACKUP_DIR"

STEP 2: VERIFY MASTER BOOTSTRAP FLAGS (Do This Before Running Ansible)

Objective: Ensure Ansible will use correct bootstrap mode

#!/bin/bash echo "=== BOOTSTRAP FLAG CHECK ===" # Check if you're doing FRESH deployment or existing cluster upgrade if [ -f "inventories/elk-prod-rhel9.yml" ]; then echo "✅ New inventory exists: elk-prod-rhel9.yml" # Check if initial_bootstrap is set grep -n "initial_bootstrap" inventories/elk-prod-rhel9.yml || echo "⚠️ initial_bootstrap NOT set (will use default=false)" echo "" echo "IMPORTANT: For FIRST deployment, add to inventory:" echo ' vars:' echo ' initial_bootstrap: true # Only first time' else echo "❌ Missing: inventories/elk-prod-rhel9.yml" echo "Create it based on inventories/elk-prod.yml with new hostnames" exit 1 fi echo "" echo "After deployment, bootstrap flag auto-resets. This is correct behavior."

STEP 3: RUN ANSIBLE DEPLOYMENT (Let Ansible Handle It)

#!/bin/bash echo "=== RUNNING ANSIBLE DEPLOYMENT ===" echo "This deploys 3 masters sequentially (serial: 1) to maintain quorum" echo "Duration: 30-45 minutes per master = 90-135 mins total" echo "" ansible-playbook install_stack.yml \ -i inventories/elk-prod-rhel9.yml \ --ask-vault-pass \ -e "install_serial=1" \ -e "initial_bootstrap=true" \ -v if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then echo "✅ Ansible deployment successful" else echo "❌ Ansible deployment failed" exit 1 fi

STEP 4: VERIFY MASTER QUORUM FORMED (Do Immediately After Ansible)

Objective: Confirm all 3 new masters elected a leader and formed cluster

#!/bin/bash PASSWORD="$ELASTICSEARCH_PASSWORD" NEW_MASTER="[NEW_PROD_MASTER_1]:9200" echo "=== MASTER QUORUM VERIFICATION ===" echo "Waiting for master election... (up to 5 minutes)" echo "" # Wait for cluster to respond ATTEMPTS=0 while [ $ATTEMPTS -lt 30 ]; do HEALTH=$(curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "https://$NEW_MASTER/_cluster/health" 2>/dev/null) if echo "$HEALTH" | jq . >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "✅ New cluster responding" break fi echo "[$ATTEMPTS/30] Waiting for cluster..." sleep 10 ((ATTEMPTS++)) done # Check master election echo "" echo "1️⃣ MASTER ELECTION:" MASTER=$(curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "https://$NEW_MASTER/_cat/master" 2>/dev/null) echo "$MASTER" if [ -z "$MASTER" ]; then echo "❌ NO MASTER ELECTED - CRITICAL ERROR" echo " Check Elasticsearch logs on new masters" exit 1 else echo "✅ Master elected successfully" fi # Check all 3 masters present echo "" echo "2️⃣ MASTER-ELIGIBLE NODES:" MASTER_COUNT=$(curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "https://$NEW_MASTER/_cat/nodes?h=roles" 2>/dev/null | grep -o '\*' | wc -l) echo "Master-eligible nodes: $MASTER_COUNT (expected: 3)" if [ "$MASTER_COUNT" -ne 3 ]; then echo "❌ CRITICAL: Expected 3 masters, found $MASTER_COUNT" echo " Check node join logs" exit 1 else echo "✅ All 3 masters present" fi # Show cluster health echo "" echo "3️⃣ CLUSTER HEALTH:" curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "https://$NEW_MASTER/_cluster/health" | \ jq '{status: .status, nodes: .number_of_nodes, unassigned_shards: .unassigned_shards}' echo "" echo "✅ Master quorum verification complete"

Success Criteria:

  • ✅ Master elected (not empty)

  • ✅ 3 master-eligible nodes present

  • ✅ Cluster health shows all nodes

If Failed:

# SSH to a new master and check logs ssh [NEW_PROD_MASTER_1] tail -100 /var/log/elasticsearch/elasticsearch.log | grep -E "master|elected|discovery" # Common issues: # - DNS not resolving (check /etc/hosts) # - Certificate TLS errors (check cert chain) # - Network connectivity (check ports 9200, 9300)

STEP 5: VERIFY DATA NODES JOINED (After Master Quorum)

Objective: Confirm all data nodes joined new master cluster

#!/bin/bash PASSWORD="$ELASTICSEARCH_PASSWORD" NEW_MASTER="[NEW_PROD_MASTER_1]:9200" echo "=== DATA NODE JOIN VERIFICATION ===" echo "Waiting for data nodes to join... (up to 10 minutes)" echo "" EXPECTED_DATA_NODES=10 # 10 hot + 5 frozen + 1 ml = 16 total, or adjust for your setup EXPECTED_TOTAL=16 # Masters(3) + Data(10) + Frozen(5) + ML(1) for i in {1..60}; do TOTAL=$(curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "https://$NEW_MASTER/_cat/nodes?h=name" 2>/dev/null | wc -l) STATUS=$(curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "https://$NEW_MASTER/_cluster/health" 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.status') echo "[$i/60] Nodes joined: $TOTAL/$EXPECTED_TOTAL, Status: $STATUS" if [ "$TOTAL" -ge "$EXPECTED_TOTAL" ] && [ "$STATUS" = "green" ]; then echo "✅ All nodes joined and cluster healthy" break fi sleep 10 done # Show node breakdown echo "" echo "NODE BREAKDOWN:" curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "https://$NEW_MASTER/_cat/nodes?h=name,roles,version" | column -t echo "" echo "CLUSTER STATUS:" curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "https://$NEW_MASTER/_cluster/health" | jq '.'

STEP 6: VERIFY SNAPSHOT RESTORE COMPLETE (After Data Nodes Join)

#!/bin/bash PASSWORD="$ELASTICSEARCH_PASSWORD" NEW_MASTER="[NEW_PROD_MASTER_1]:9200" echo "=== SNAPSHOT RESTORE VERIFICATION ===" # Check if restore in progress echo "1️⃣ RESTORE STATUS:" curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "https://$NEW_MASTER/_cat/recovery" 2>/dev/null | head -20 echo "" echo "2️⃣ UNSTARTED SHARDS (should be 0):" UNSTARTED=$(curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "https://$NEW_MASTER/_cat/shards?format=json" 2>/dev/null | jq '[.[] | select(.state != "STARTED")] | length') echo "Unstarted shards: $UNSTARTED" if [ "$UNSTARTED" -gt 0 ]; then echo "⚠️ Still recovering... check back in 5 minutes" else echo "✅ All shards started" fi echo "" echo "3️⃣ DOCUMENT COUNT:" curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "https://$NEW_MASTER/_stats" 2>/dev/null | jq '.indices._all.primaries.docs.count'

STEP 7: VERIFY NO CLUSTER MERGE (Old + New Separate)

Objective: Ensure old and new clusters are NOT merging (they should be separate)

#!/bin/bash PASSWORD="$ELASTICSEARCH_PASSWORD" echo "=== CLUSTER SEPARATION VERIFICATION ===" echo "Old and new clusters must remain separate (no auto-discovery)" echo "" # Count nodes in OLD cluster echo "OLD CLUSTER (prod):" OLD_NODES=$(curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200/_cat/nodes?h=name" 2>/dev/null | wc -l) echo "Nodes: $OLD_NODES" # Count nodes in NEW cluster echo "" echo "NEW CLUSTER (RHEL9):" NEW_NODES=$(curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "https://[NEW_PROD_MASTER_1]:9200/_cat/nodes?h=name" 2>/dev/null | wc -l) echo "Nodes: $NEW_NODES" # Total should be old + new, NOT merged TOTAL=$((OLD_NODES + NEW_NODES)) echo "" echo "TOTAL: $OLD_NODES (old) + $NEW_NODES (new) = $TOTAL" echo "If merged, total would be $((OLD_NODES + NEW_NODES))/2" echo "" if [ "$TOTAL" -eq $((OLD_NODES + NEW_NODES)) ]; then echo "✅ Clusters are SEPARATE (correct)" else echo "❌ Clusters may have MERGED (check cluster names)" fi # Verify cluster names are DIFFERENT echo "" echo "CLUSTER NAME CHECK:" OLD_NAME=$(curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200/_cluster/health" 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.cluster_name') NEW_NAME=$(curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "https://[NEW_PROD_MASTER_1]:9200/_cluster/health" 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.cluster_name') echo "Old cluster name: $OLD_NAME" echo "New cluster name: $NEW_NAME" if [ "$OLD_NAME" != "$NEW_NAME" ]; then echo "✅ Different cluster names (correct)" else echo "⚠️ Same cluster name - may have merged" fi

STEP 8: TAKE CLUSTER STATE SNAPSHOT (Before Cutover)

Objective: Back up new cluster state before updating services

#!/bin/bash PASSWORD="$ELASTICSEARCH_PASSWORD" BACKUP_DIR="/tmp/cluster-backups" mkdir -p "$BACKUP_DIR" echo "=== TAKING FINAL CLUSTER STATE SNAPSHOT ===" # Snapshot of NEW cluster curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD \ https://[NEW_PROD_MASTER_1]:9200/_cluster/state \ > "$BACKUP_DIR/NEW-cluster-state-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).json" # Node info curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD \ https://[NEW_PROD_MASTER_1]:9200/_cat/nodes?v \ > "$BACKUP_DIR/NEW-nodes-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).txt" # Shard allocation curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD \ https://[NEW_PROD_MASTER_1]:9200/_cat/shards?v \ > "$BACKUP_DIR/NEW-shards-after-restore.txt" # Indices curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD \ https://[NEW_PROD_MASTER_1]:9200/_cat/indices?v \ > "$BACKUP_DIR/NEW-indices-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).txt" echo "✅ Snapshots saved to: $BACKUP_DIR" ls -la "$BACKUP_DIR" | tail -5

STEP 9: VERIFY OLD CLUSTER STILL HEALTHY (Critical Safety Check)

Objective: Confirm old cluster hasn't been affected by new deployment

#!/bin/bash PASSWORD="$ELASTICSEARCH_PASSWORD" echo "=== OLD CLUSTER HEALTH CHECK ===" echo "1️⃣ CLUSTER STATUS:" curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200/_cluster/health" | jq '{status, nodes: .number_of_nodes}' echo "" echo "2️⃣ MASTER NODES (should still be 3):" MASTER_COUNT=$(curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200/_cat/nodes?h=roles" 2>/dev/null | grep -o '\*' | wc -l) echo "Master-eligible nodes: $MASTER_COUNT" if [ "$MASTER_COUNT" -ne 3 ]; then echo "❌ CRITICAL: Old cluster lost masters!" exit 1 fi echo "" echo "3️⃣ SERVICES STILL USING OLD CLUSTER:" netstat -an | grep -E "evelkmnp.*:9200" | grep ESTABLISHED echo " (If nothing shows, need to add process monitoring)" echo "" echo "✅ Old cluster still healthy (safe to proceed with cutover)"

STEP 10: MANUAL CUTOVER VERIFICATION (Before Running Step 4.6)

#!/bin/bash echo "=== PRE-CUTOVER CHECKLIST ===" echo "" echo "Before updating Logstash/Kibana/Fleet to new masters, verify:" echo "" # Yes/No prompts read -p "1. Are all 3 new master nodes running and elected? (y/n) " -n 1 -r echo "" if [[ ! $REPLY =~ ^[Yy]$ ]]; then echo "❌ Stop - fix masters first"; exit 1; fi read -p "2. Is new cluster health GREEN? (y/n) " -n 1 -r echo "" if [[ ! $REPLY =~ ^[Yy]$ ]]; then echo "❌ Stop - wait for cluster to recover"; exit 1; fi read -p "3. Have all documents been restored? (y/n) " -n 1 -r echo "" if [[ ! $REPLY =~ ^[Yy]$ ]]; then echo "❌ Stop - wait for restore to complete"; exit 1; fi read -p "4. Is old cluster still running and healthy? (y/n) " -n 1 -r echo "" if [[ ! $REPLY =~ ^[Yy]$ ]]; then echo "❌ Stop - do not cut over if old cluster is unhealthy"; exit 1; fi read -p "5. Have you backed up cluster state files? (y/n) " -n 1 -r echo "" if [[ ! $REPLY =~ ^[Yy]$ ]]; then echo "❌ Stop - back up first"; exit 1; fi echo "" echo "✅ ALL CHECKS PASSED - Safe to proceed to Step 4.6 (Cutover)"

4.3 Step 3: Deploy ELK 8.18.1 to New RHEL9 Servers Using Ansible

Assuming new RHEL9 servers are already provisioned and SSH-accessible with Ansible inventory configured:

#!/bin/bash # Deploy entire ELK stack to new RHEL9 infrastructure # install_serial=1 ensures masters deploy sequentially (maintains old cluster quorum) ansible-playbook install_stack.yml \ -i inventories/elk-prod-rhel9.yml \ --ask-vault-pass \ -e "install_serial=1" \ -v # What install_stack.yml does: # - Installs Elasticsearch 8.18.1 on all elasticsearch hosts # - Configures node roles, discovery, TLS settings # (masters: node.roles: [master]) # (data: node.roles: [data_content,data_hot,data_warm,data_cold,ingest,etc]) # - Installs Kibana 8.18.1, configures OIDC/ADFS # - Installs Logstash 8.18.1, deploys pipelines # - Installs Fleet Server / Elastic Agent 8.18.1 # Verify new Elasticsearch cluster is formed (separate from old cluster) sleep 30 echo "Verifying new cluster..." curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD https://[NEW_PROD_MASTER_1]:9200/_cluster/health | \ jq '{status, nodes: .number_of_nodes, active_shards: .active_shards, active_primary_shards: .active_primary_shards}' # Verify all 3 masters elected echo "Master nodes:" curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD https://[NEW_PROD_MASTER_1]:9200/_cat/nodes | grep master

4.4 Step 4: Restore Snapshot to New RHEL9 Cluster

#!/bin/bash NEW_ENDPOINT="https://[NEW_PROD_MASTER_1]:9200" PASSWORD="$ELASTICSEARCH_PASSWORD" REPO="isilon" SNAPSHOT_ID="rhel9-pre-migration-20260709-123456" # From step 2 echo "Registering snapshot repository on NEW cluster..." curl -X PUT "$NEW_ENDPOINT/_snapshot/$REPO" \ -u elastic:$PASSWORD \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "type": "fs", "settings": { "location": "/mnt/snapshots/prod", "readonly": false } }' echo "Restoring snapshot to NEW RHEL9 cluster (may take 10-60+ minutes)..." curl -X POST "$NEW_ENDPOINT/_snapshot/$REPO/$SNAPSHOT_ID/_restore" \ -u elastic:$PASSWORD \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "indices": "*", "include_global_state": true, "partial": false }' # Monitor restore for i in {1..360}; do HEALTH=$(curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "$NEW_ENDPOINT/_cluster/health" 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.status') UNSTARTED=$(curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "$NEW_ENDPOINT/_cat/shards?format=json" 2>/dev/null | jq '[.[] | select(.state != "STARTED")] | length') echo "[$i/360] Health: $HEALTH, Unstarted shards: $UNSTARTED" [ "$HEALTH" = "green" ] && echo "✅ Restore complete" && break sleep 10 done

4.5 Step 5: Validate New RHEL9 Cluster Before Cutover

#!/bin/bash NEW_ENDPOINT="https://[NEW_PROD_MASTER_1]:9200" PASSWORD="$ELASTICSEARCH_PASSWORD" echo "=== NEW RHEL9 CLUSTER VALIDATION ===" echo "1. Cluster health:" curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "$NEW_ENDPOINT/_cluster/health" | \ jq '{status, nodes: .number_of_nodes, active_shards: .active_shards, unassigned_shards: .unassigned_shards}' echo "" echo "2. Master node quorum (must be 3):" MASTER_COUNT=$(curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "$NEW_ENDPOINT/_cat/nodes?h=roles" | grep -o '\*' | wc -l) echo "Master-eligible nodes: $MASTER_COUNT (expected: 3)" curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "$NEW_ENDPOINT/_cat/nodes?h=name,roles,version" echo "" echo "3. All nodes 8.18.1:" curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "$NEW_ENDPOINT/_cat/nodes?h=name,version" echo "" echo "4. Data nodes by role:" curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "$NEW_ENDPOINT/_cat/nodes?h=name,roles" | tail -16 echo "" echo "5. Document count:" curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "$NEW_ENDPOINT/_stats" | jq '.indices._all.primaries.docs.count' echo "" echo "6. Indices status (sample first 40):" curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "$NEW_ENDPOINT/_cat/indices?v" | head -40 echo "" echo "7. Verify NO auto-discovery between old and new clusters:" echo " Old cluster (prod) nodes:" curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200/_cat/nodes?h=name | wc -l echo " New cluster (RHEL9) nodes:" curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "$NEW_ENDPOINT/_cat/nodes?h=name" | wc -l echo " (Should be 9 old + 9 new = 18 total across BOTH clusters, not 9 in one)"

4.6 Step 6: Cutover - Update All Services to Point to New Elasticsearch

Update Logstash outputs to new Elasticsearch:

ansible-playbook install_stack.yml \ -i inventories/elk-prod-rhel9.yml \ --ask-vault-pass \ -e "role_list=['logstash']" \ -e "elasticsearch_hosts=['[NEW_PROD_MASTER_1]:9200','[NEW_PROD_MASTER_2]:9200','[NEW_PROD_MASTER_3]:9200']" \ -v

Update Kibana to connect to new Elasticsearch:

ansible-playbook install_stack.yml \ -i inventories/elk-prod-rhel9.yml \ --ask-vault-pass \ -e "role_list=['kibana']" \ -e "elasticsearch_hosts=['[NEW_PROD_MASTER_1]:9200','[NEW_PROD_MASTER_2]:9200','[NEW_PROD_MASTER_3]:9200']" \ -v

Update Fleet outputs to new Elasticsearch:

ansible-playbook install_stack.yml \ -i inventories/elk-prod-rhel9.yml \ --ask-vault-pass \ -e "role_list=['fleet']" \ -e "elasticsearch_hosts=['[NEW_PROD_MASTER_1]:9200','[NEW_PROD_MASTER_2]:9200','[NEW_PROD_MASTER_3]:9200']" \ -v

Update DNS/Load Balancers (Manual):

  • Switch kibana.elk.omf.cloud DNS → new Kibana IPs

  • Switch Logstash LB backends → new Logstash IPs

  • Switch Elasticsearch VIP/DNS → new Master IPs (if used)

4.7 Step 7: Decommission Old Production Elasticsearch Servers

⚠️ Master Node Decommissioning (CRITICAL)

DO NOT decommission old master nodes (evelkmnp01/02/03) until:

  1. New cluster has run for 7+ days with all indices healthy

  2. Confirm NO services are connecting to old cluster (use netstat monitoring)

  3. Verify DNS/LB points exclusively to new masters ([NEW_PROD_MASTER_1-3])

  4. Take final backup of old cluster to S3 (isilon repo)

#!/bin/bash echo "=== OLD MASTER NODE DECOMMISSIONING SAFETY CHECKS ===" OLD_MASTER="evelkmnp01.corp.fin" echo "1. Check if any services still connecting to old cluster:" ssh $OLD_MASTER sudo netstat -an | grep -E '9200|9300' | grep ESTABLISHED echo "" echo "2. Verify old cluster status (should show old 9-node cluster):" curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD https://$OLD_MASTER:9200/_cluster/health | \ jq '{status, nodes: .number_of_nodes}' echo "" echo "3. Before decommissioning, do FINAL backup:" FINAL_SNAPSHOT=$(curl -X PUT "https://$OLD_MASTER:9200/_snapshot/isilon/final-rhel7-backup-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)" \ -u elastic:$PASSWORD -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{ "indices": "*", "include_global_state": true }' | jq -r '.snapshot // "error"') echo "Final snapshot: $FINAL_SNAPSHOT" echo "Wait for completion..." # Wait for snapshot for i in {1..120}; do STATE=$(curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "https://$OLD_MASTER:9200/_snapshot/isilon/$FINAL_SNAPSHOT/_status" | jq -r '.snapshots[0].state // "pending"') [ "$STATE" = "SUCCESS" ] && echo "✅ Final backup complete" && break sleep 10 done

Safe Decommissioning Process

Only after above checks pass:

#!/bin/bash echo "Decommissioning old Elasticsearch servers..." echo "⚠️ Only after new cluster has been stable for 7+ days" # Remove old masters from DNS/LB first echo "1. Verify DNS points to new cluster only:" nslookup elasticsearch.elk.omf.cloud # Should resolve to [NEW_PROD_MASTER_*] IPs only # Then disable shards on old cluster echo "" echo "2. Disable shard allocation on OLD cluster (graceful shutdown):" curl -X PUT "https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200/_cluster/settings" \ -u elastic:$PASSWORD \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "persistent": { "cluster.routing.allocation.enable": "none" } }' # Use Ansible to stop services on old servers echo "" echo "3. Stop Elasticsearch on all old servers:" ansible elasticsearch -i inventories/elk-prod.yml \ --ask-vault-pass \ -m service \ -a "name=elasticsearch state=stopped enabled=no" \ -b # Archive old configurations for rollback window echo "" echo "4. Archive old configurations (keep for 90 days):" ansible elasticsearch -i inventories/elk-prod.yml \ -m shell \ -a "tar -czf /opt/elasticsearch-backup-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz /etc/elasticsearch /var/lib/elasticsearch" \ -b echo "✅ Old servers archived and stopped" echo "Keep running for 7+ day rollback window before full decommission"

7-Day Monitoring Checklist (Before Final Decommission)

Do this EVERY DAY for 7 days after cutover:

#!/bin/bash PASSWORD="$ELASTICSEARCH_PASSWORD" echo "=== 7-DAY MONITORING CHECKLIST (Run Daily) ===" DATE=$(date +%Y-%m-%d) LOG_FILE="/tmp/migration-monitoring-$DATE.log" { echo "=== Daily Monitoring: $DATE ===" echo "" echo "1. NEW CLUSTER HEALTH:" curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD https://[NEW_PROD_MASTER_1]:9200/_cluster/health | jq '.{status, nodes: .number_of_nodes, unassigned_shards}' echo "" echo "2. DOCUMENT COUNT (should be stable):" curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD https://[NEW_PROD_MASTER_1]:9200/_stats | jq '.indices._all.primaries.docs.count' echo "" echo "3. SHARD ALLOCATION (should be 0 unstarted):" curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "https://[NEW_PROD_MASTER_1]:9200/_cat/shards?format=json" | jq '[.[] | select(.state != "STARTED")] | length' echo "" echo "4. LOGSTASH INDEXING (events flowing):" curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "https://[NEW_PROD_MASTER_1]:9200/_stats" | jq '.indices | keys[] | select(startswith("logstash-")) | .' | head -5 echo "" echo "5. NO ERRORS IN LOGS (sample):" ssh [NEW_PROD_MASTER_1] "tail -50 /var/log/elasticsearch/elasticsearch.log | grep -i error | wc -l" echo "" echo "6. KIBANA ACCESSIBLE:" curl -s -I https://kibana.elk.omf.cloud | head -1 echo "" echo "=== Monitoring Complete: $DATE ===" } | tee -a "$LOG_FILE" echo "Log saved to: $LOG_FILE"

Conditions to STOP Decommissioning If Any Occur:

  • ❌ Cluster status != GREEN for >1 hour

  • ❌ Unassigned shards > 0 for >1 hour

  • ❌ Document count DECREASES

  • ❌ Logstash stops indexing

  • ❌ Kibana becomes inaccessible

  • ❌ ANY errors in Elasticsearch logs related to cluster state

If ANY of above occur: STOP and investigate before proceeding.

Final Pre-Decommission Master Node Checklist

Run this EXACTLY 7 days after cutover:

#!/bin/bash PASSWORD="$ELASTICSEARCH_PASSWORD" echo "=== FINAL PRE-DECOMMISSION CHECKLIST (Day 7+) ===" echo "" # 1. Verify new cluster is stable echo "1️⃣ NEW CLUSTER 7-DAY STABILITY CHECK:" HEALTH=$(curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD https://[NEW_PROD_MASTER_1]:9200/_cluster/health | jq '.status') echo "Status: $HEALTH" if [ "$HEALTH" != '"green"' ]; then echo "❌ STOP - Cluster not GREEN" exit 1 fi # 2. Verify all services switched to new masters echo "" echo "2️⃣ SERVICE VERIFICATION:" echo " Checking if Logstash is pointing to NEW masters..." grep "elasticsearch_host" /etc/logstash/conf.d/*.conf | head -3 echo "" echo " Checking if Kibana is pointing to NEW masters..." grep "elasticsearch.hosts" /etc/kibana/kibana.yml echo "" echo " Checking if Fleet is pointing to NEW masters..." grep "elasticsearch.hosts" /etc/fleet-server/fleet-server.yml 2>/dev/null || echo " (Fleet uses agents, check via Kibana)" # 3. Verify DNS points to new masters echo "" echo "3️⃣ DNS VERIFICATION:" nslookup elasticsearch.elk.omf.cloud | grep "Address:" # 4. Verify NO connections from old cluster echo "" echo "4️⃣ OLD CLUSTER CONNECTION CHECK:" for OLD_MASTER in evelkmnp01.corp.fin evelkmnp02.corp.fin evelkmnp03.corp.fin; do CONNECTIONS=$(ssh $OLD_MASTER "netstat -an 2>/dev/null | grep 9200 | grep ESTABLISHED | wc -l" 2>/dev/null) echo " $OLD_MASTER: $CONNECTIONS active connections (should be 0)" done # 5. Take final backup echo "" echo "5️⃣ FINAL BACKUP OF OLD CLUSTER:" read -p " Ready to take final snapshot? (y/n) " -n 1 -r echo if [[ $REPLY =~ ^[Yy]$ ]]; then SNAPSHOT_ID="final-backup-before-decommission-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)" curl -X PUT "https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200/_snapshot/isilon/$SNAPSHOT_ID" \ -u elastic:$PASSWORD -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{ "indices": "*", "include_global_state": true }' echo " Snapshot: $SNAPSHOT_ID" echo " Wait for completion before proceeding..." fi # 6. Final safety prompt echo "" echo "6️⃣ FINAL AUTHORIZATION:" read -p " Have you confirmed all 6 checks above? Type 'DECOMMISSION' to proceed: " CONFIRM if [ "$CONFIRM" != "DECOMMISSION" ]; then echo "❌ Decommission cancelled" exit 1 fi echo "" echo "✅ ALL CHECKS PASSED - Safe to proceed with decommissioning"

Master Node Decommissioning Steps (After All Checks Pass)

Step 1: Disable Shard Allocation on Old Cluster

#!/bin/bash PASSWORD="$ELASTICSEARCH_PASSWORD" echo "=== STEP 1: DISABLE SHARD ALLOCATION ===" curl -X PUT "https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200/_cluster/settings" \ -u elastic:$PASSWORD \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "persistent": { "cluster.routing.allocation.enable": "none" } }' | jq '.' echo "" echo "✅ Shard allocation disabled - cluster in graceful shutdown mode"

Step 2: Exclude Old Masters from Voting (Optional but Recommended)

#!/bin/bash PASSWORD="$ELASTICSEARCH_PASSWORD" echo "=== STEP 2: EXCLUDE OLD MASTERS FROM VOTING ===" echo "This prevents old masters from trying to elect if they accidentally rejoin" echo "" # On NEW cluster, exclude OLD masters from voting curl -X PUT "https://[NEW_PROD_MASTER_1]:9200/_cluster/voting_config_exclusions?node_names=evelkmnp01,evelkmnp02,evelkmnp03&timeout=30s" \ -u elastic:$PASSWORD echo "" echo "✅ Old masters excluded from voting"

Step 3: Stop Elasticsearch on Old Master Nodes

#!/bin/bash echo "=== STEP 3: STOP ELASTICSEARCH ON OLD MASTERS ===" # Use Ansible to stop cleanly ansible elasticsearch -i inventories/elk-prod.yml \ --limit "evelkmnp01.corp.fin,evelkmnp02.corp.fin,evelkmnp03.corp.fin" \ --ask-vault-pass \ -m service \ -a "name=elasticsearch state=stopped enabled=no" \ -b echo "" echo "✅ Old Elasticsearch services stopped"

Step 4: Archive Old Configurations

#!/bin/bash echo "=== STEP 4: ARCHIVE OLD CONFIGURATIONS ===" # Archive on each old master for 90-day rollback window ansible elasticsearch -i inventories/elk-prod.yml \ --limit "evelkmnp01.corp.fin,evelkmnp02.corp.fin,evelkmnp03.corp.fin" \ -m shell \ -a "tar -czf /opt/elasticsearch-backup-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz /etc/elasticsearch /var/lib/elasticsearch && ls -lh /opt/elasticsearch-backup-*.tar.gz" \ -b echo "" echo "✅ Old configurations backed up (keep for 90 days for rollback)"

Step 5: Final Verification

#!/bin/bash PASSWORD="$ELASTICSEARCH_PASSWORD" echo "=== STEP 5: FINAL VERIFICATION ===" echo "1. NEW CLUSTER STATUS:" curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD https://[NEW_PROD_MASTER_1]:9200/_cluster/health | jq '.' echo "" echo "2. OLD CLUSTER STATUS (should be red/unresponsive):" curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200/_cluster/health 2>&1 || echo " (Connection refused - expected)" echo "" echo "3. VERIFY NO LOGSTASH ERRORS:" tail -20 /var/log/logstash/logstash-plain.log | grep -i error echo "" echo "✅ Decommissioning complete" echo "" echo "NEXT STEPS:" echo " - Keep old servers offline for 7 more days as rollback window" echo " - After day 14: Can fully decommission or repurpose hardware" echo " - Monitor new cluster for any issues during this period"

Rollback Procedure (If Something Goes Wrong)

If you encounter critical issues within 7 days:

#!/bin/bash PASSWORD="$ELASTICSEARCH_PASSWORD" echo "=== EMERGENCY ROLLBACK PROCEDURE ===" echo "" echo "⚠️ Only use if NEW cluster has critical issues" echo "" # Step 1: Start old cluster back up echo "STEP 1: Restarting old Elasticsearch services..." ansible elasticsearch -i inventories/elk-prod.yml \ --limit "evelkmnp01.corp.fin,evelkmnp02.corp.fin,evelkmnp03.corp.fin" \ --ask-vault-pass \ -m service \ -a "name=elasticsearch state=started enabled=yes" \ -b sleep 60 # Step 2: Wait for old cluster to form quorum echo "" echo "STEP 2: Waiting for old cluster to elect master..." for i in {1..30}; do MASTER=$(curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200/_cat/master" 2>/dev/null) if [ -n "$MASTER" ]; then echo "✅ Master elected" break fi echo "[$i/30] Waiting for master election..." sleep 10 done # Step 3: Re-enable shard allocation echo "" echo "STEP 3: Re-enabling shard allocation..." curl -X PUT "https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200/_cluster/settings" \ -u elastic:$PASSWORD \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "persistent": { "cluster.routing.allocation.enable": null } }' | jq '.acknowledged' # Step 4: Redirect services back to old cluster echo "" echo "STEP 4: Update services to point back to old masters" echo " - Update Logstash elasticsearch_hosts to old masters" echo " - Update Kibana elasticsearch.hosts to old masters" echo " - Update Fleet elasticsearch hosts to old masters" echo "" echo "✅ Rollback complete - cluster restored to old state" echo "" echo "Then investigate what went wrong with new cluster before retry"

5. Logstash Migration Using Ansible

5.1 Deploy New RHEL9 Logstash Servers

Ensure new RHEL9 Logstash servers are added to inventories/elk-prod-rhel9.yml:

logstash: vars: logstash_pipeline_ids: [ "input_*","output_*","parser_*","routing","dead_letter_queue","end_processor" ] logstash_env_variables: # Copy all from elk-prod.yml hosts: [NEW_PROD_LOGSTASH_01]: logstash_heap_size: 64g logstash_direct_memory_size: 32g # ... (01-12)

Deploy Logstash 8.18.1 to all new RHEL9 servers:

#!/bin/bash ansible-playbook install_stack.yml \ -i inventories/elk-prod-rhel9.yml \ --ask-vault-pass \ -e "role_list=['logstash']" \ -e "elasticsearch_hosts=['[NEW_PROD_MASTER_1]:9200','[NEW_PROD_MASTER_2]:9200','[NEW_PROD_MASTER_3]:9200']" \ -v

5.2 Validate Logstash Pipelines

#!/bin/bash echo "=== LOGSTASH RHEL9 VALIDATION ===" for i in {01..12}; do host="[NEW_PROD_LOGSTASH_$i]" echo "Checking $host..." # Version curl -s http://$host:9600/ 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.version.number // "error"' # Pipeline status curl -s http://$host:9600/_node/stats/pipelines | \ jq '.pipelines[] | {name: .name, events_in: .events.in, events_out: .events.out}' done echo "✅ Logstash validation complete"

5.3 Decommission Old Logstash Servers

#!/bin/bash echo "Decommissioning old RHEL7 Logstash servers..." echo "⚠️ After new RHEL9 Logstash is stable (7+ days)" ansible logstash -i inventories/elk-prod.yml \ --ask-vault-pass \ -m service \ -a "name=logstash state=stopped enabled=no" \ -b echo "✅ Old Logstash servers stopped"

6. Kibana Migration Using Ansible

6.1 Deploy New RHEL9 Kibana Servers

Ensure new RHEL9 Kibana servers are in inventories/elk-prod-rhel9.yml:

kibana: vars: kibana_public_host: kibana.elk.omf.cloud kibana_encryption_key: !vault | [COPY FROM elk-prod.yml] hosts: [NEW_PROD_KIBANA_1]: [NEW_PROD_KIBANA_2]:

Deploy Kibana 8.18.1:

#!/bin/bash ansible-playbook install_stack.yml \ -i inventories/elk-prod-rhel9.yml \ --ask-vault-pass \ -e "role_list=['kibana']" \ -e "elasticsearch_hosts=['[NEW_PROD_MASTER_1]:9200','[NEW_PROD_MASTER_2]:9200','[NEW_PROD_MASTER_3]:9200']" \ -v

6.2 Validate Kibana

#!/bin/bash KIBANA="https://[NEW_PROD_KIBANA_1]:5601" AUTH="-u elastic:$PASSWORD" echo "=== KIBANA RHEL9 VALIDATION ===" echo "Status:" curl -s $AUTH "$KIBANA/api/status" | jq '.status.overall.state' echo "" echo "Dashboards:" curl -s $AUTH "$KIBANA/api/saved_objects/_find?type=dashboard" | jq '.total' echo "" echo "Alerts:" curl -s $AUTH "$KIBANA/api/alerting/rules/_find" | jq '.total' echo "" echo "Authentication:" curl -s $AUTH "$KIBANA/api/security/me" | jq '{username: .username, roles: .roles}' echo "✅ Kibana validation complete"

6.3 Update DNS/Load Balancer

Switch kibana.elk.omf.cloud to point to new RHEL9 Kibana nodes.

6.4 Decommission Old Kibana

#!/bin/bash ansible kibana -i inventories/elk-prod.yml \ --ask-vault-pass \ -m service \ -a "name=kibana state=stopped enabled=no" \ -b echo "✅ Old Kibana stopped"

7. Fleet & Beats Migration Using Ansible

7.1 Deploy New RHEL9 Fleet Servers

Ensure new RHEL9 Fleet servers are in inventories/elk-prod-rhel9.yml:

fleet: hosts: [NEW_PROD_FLEET_1]: [NEW_PROD_FLEET_2]:

Deploy Fleet Server / Elastic Agent 8.18.1:

#!/bin/bash ansible-playbook install_stack.yml \ -i inventories/elk-prod-rhel9.yml \ --ask-vault-pass \ -e "role_list=['fleet']" \ -e "elasticsearch_hosts=['[NEW_PROD_MASTER_1]:9200','[NEW_PROD_MASTER_2]:9200','[NEW_PROD_MASTER_3]:9200']" \ -v

7.2 Validate Fleet & Agents

#!/bin/bash FLEET_HOST="[NEW_PROD_FLEET_1]" NEW_ENDPOINT="https://[NEW_PROD_MASTER_1]:9200" echo "=== FLEET RHEL9 VALIDATION ===" echo "Fleet status:" curl -s https://$FLEET_HOST:8220/api/status 2>/dev/null | jq echo "" echo "Agent enrollment status:" curl -s https://$FLEET_HOST:8220/api/fleet/agents | \ jq '[.items[] | .agent.status] | group_by(.) | map({status: .[0], count: length})' echo "" echo "Data flowing to ES:" echo "Logs:" curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "$NEW_ENDPOINT/logs-*/_search" | jq '.hits.total.value' echo "Metrics:" curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD "$NEW_ENDPOINT/metrics-*/_search" | jq '.hits.total.value' echo "✅ Fleet validation complete"

7.3 Decommission Old Fleet

#!/bin/bash ansible fleet -i inventories/elk-prod.yml \ --ask-vault-pass \ -m service \ -a "name=elastic-agent state=stopped enabled=no" \ -b echo "✅ Old Fleet stopped"

8. Post-Upgrade Validation

Comprehensive Validation Script

#!/bin/bash ENDPOINT="https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200" AUTH="-u elastic:$PASSWORD" PASS_COUNT=0 FAIL_COUNT=0 WARN_COUNT=0 echo "╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗" echo "║ RHEL9 UPGRADE - COMPREHENSIVE VALIDATION SUITE ║" echo "║ Starting: $(date +'%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') ║" echo "╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝" echo "" # ============ ELASTICSEARCH CHECKS ============ echo "[1/7] ELASTICSEARCH CLUSTER HEALTH..." HEALTH=$(curl -s $AUTH "$ENDPOINT/_cluster/health") STATUS=$(echo $HEALTH | jq -r '.status') NODES=$(echo $HEALTH | jq '.number_of_nodes') UNASSIGNED=$(echo $HEALTH | jq '.unassigned_shards') echo " Status: $STATUS (expected: green)" echo " Nodes: $NODES (expected: 9-10)" echo " Unassigned shards: $UNASSIGNED (expected: 0)" if [ "$STATUS" = "green" ] && [ "$UNASSIGNED" = "0" ]; then echo " ✅ PASS" ((PASS_COUNT++)) else echo " ❌ FAIL" ((FAIL_COUNT++)) fi # ============ NODE VERSIONS ============ echo "" echo "[2/7] NODE VERSIONS..." NODES_UPGRADED=$(curl -s $AUTH "$ENDPOINT/_cat/nodes?h=version" | grep -c "8.18.1") TOTAL_NODES=$(curl -s $AUTH "$ENDPOINT/_cat/nodes?h=version" | wc -l) echo " Upgraded: $NODES_UPGRADED/$TOTAL_NODES" if [ "$NODES_UPGRADED" -eq "$TOTAL_NODES" ]; then echo " ✅ PASS - All nodes are 8.18.1" ((PASS_COUNT++)) else echo " ❌ FAIL - Some nodes on old version" ((FAIL_COUNT++)) fi # ============ DATA INTEGRITY ============ echo "" echo "[3/7] DATA INTEGRITY..." CURRENT_DOCS=$(curl -s $AUTH "$ENDPOINT/_stats" | jq '.indices._all.primaries.docs.count') echo " Current documents: $CURRENT_DOCS" if [ "$CURRENT_DOCS" -gt 0 ]; then echo " ✅ PASS - Documents present" ((PASS_COUNT++)) else echo " ❌ FAIL - No documents!" ((FAIL_COUNT++)) fi # ============ KIBANA ============ echo "" echo "[4/7] KIBANA..." KIBANA_STATUS=$(curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD https://evelkkbp01.corp.fin:5601/api/status 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.elasticsearch.status // "error"') echo " ES Connection: $KIBANA_STATUS" if [ "$KIBANA_STATUS" = "green" ]; then echo " ✅ PASS - Kibana connected" ((PASS_COUNT++)) else echo " ⚠️ WARNING - Kibana check unclear" ((WARN_COUNT++)) fi # ============ LOGSTASH ============ echo "" echo "[5/7] LOGSTASH..." LOGSTASH_VERSION=$(curl -s http://evelklsp01.corp.fin:9600/ 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.version.number // "error"') echo " Version: $LOGSTASH_VERSION" if [ "$LOGSTASH_VERSION" = "8.18.1" ]; then echo " ✅ PASS" ((PASS_COUNT++)) else echo " ⚠️ WARNING" ((WARN_COUNT++)) fi # ============ FLEET ============ echo "" echo "[6/7] FLEET..." FLEET_STATUS=$(curl -s https://evelkftp01.corp.fin:8220/api/status 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.state // "error"') echo " Status: $FLEET_STATUS" if [ "$FLEET_STATUS" = "running" ] || [ "$FLEET_STATUS" = "healthy" ]; then echo " ✅ PASS" ((PASS_COUNT++)) else echo " ⚠️ WARNING" ((WARN_COUNT++)) fi # ============ MACHINE LEARNING ============ echo "" echo "[7/7] MACHINE LEARNING..." ML_MODE=$(curl -s $AUTH "$ENDPOINT/_ml/set_upgrade_mode" 2>/dev/null | jq '.enabled') echo " ML Upgrade Mode: $ML_MODE (expected: false)" if [ "$ML_MODE" = "false" ]; then echo " ✅ PASS" ((PASS_COUNT++)) else echo " ⚠️ WARNING" ((WARN_COUNT++)) fi # ============ SUMMARY ============ echo "" echo "╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗" echo "║ VALIDATION SUMMARY ║" echo "╠════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣" echo "║ ✅ PASSED: $PASS_COUNT/7 ║" echo "║ ❌ FAILED: $FAIL_COUNT/7 ║" echo "║ ⚠️ WARNING: $WARN_COUNT/7 ║" echo "╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝" echo "" if [ $FAIL_COUNT -eq 0 ]; then echo "✅ UPGRADE SUCCESSFUL" exit 0 else echo "❌ UPGRADE VALIDATION FAILED" exit 1 fi

9. Troubleshooting & Emergency

Common Issues & Solutions

Issue 1: Cluster Stuck in YELLOW Status

Symptoms:

Cluster health status: yellow Unassigned shards present Duration: >15 minutes

Solution:

#!/bin/bash # Check disk space ansible elasticsearch -i inventories/elk-prod.yml \ -m shell -a "df -h /var/lib/elasticsearch" # Re-enable shard allocation curl -X PUT https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200/_cluster/settings \ -u elastic:$PASSWORD \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"persistent": {"cluster.routing.allocation.enable": null}}' # Monitor watch -n 10 'curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200/_cluster/health | jq "{status, unassigned: .unassigned_shards}"'

Issue 2: Node Won't Rejoin Cluster

Solution:

#!/bin/bash NODE="evelkwhp01.corp.fin" # Restart Elasticsearch ssh $NODE sudo systemctl restart elasticsearch # Wait 30 seconds and verify from cluster sleep 30 curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200/_cat/nodes | grep $NODE # Check certificate expiration if still failing ssh $NODE openssl x509 -in /etc/elasticsearch/certs/elasticsearch.crt -text -noout | grep -A2 "Validity"

Issue 3: Master Quorum Loss (CRITICAL)

⚠️ Requires immediate action:

#!/bin/bash echo "⚠️ CRITICAL RECOVERY - DO NOT ABORT" # Restart all masters for node in evelkmnp01 evelkmnp02 evelkmnp03; do echo "Restarting $node..." ssh $node.corp.fin sudo systemctl restart elasticsearch & done wait # Monitor recovery sleep 30 for i in {1..60}; do STATUS=$(curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200/_cluster/health 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.status // "unknown"') NODES=$(curl -s -u elastic:$PASSWORD https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200/_cat/nodes 2>/dev/null | wc -l) echo "[$i/60] Status: $STATUS, Nodes: $NODES" if [ "$STATUS" = "green" ]; then echo "✅ Cluster recovered" break fi sleep 10 done

Issue 4: Logstash Can't Connect to Elasticsearch

Solution:

# Verify ES is accessible ssh evelklsp01.corp.fin curl -u elastic:$PASSWORD https://evelkwhp01.corp.fin:9200/_cluster/health # Check if password expired - update vault ansible-vault edit group_vars/all/es_passwords.yml # Redeploy Logstash config ansible-playbook install_stack.yml -i inventories/elk-prod.yml \ --ask-vault-pass \ -e "role_list=['logstash']" \ --limit "logstash" \ -v # Restart Logstash ssh evelklsp01.corp.fin sudo systemctl restart logstash

Issue 5: Kibana Can't Connect to Elasticsearch

Solution:

# Restart Kibana ssh evelkkbp01.corp.fin sudo systemctl restart kibana # Wait 60 seconds sleep 60 # Verify connectivity curl -s https://evelkkbp01.corp.fin:5601/app/kibana | head -20 # If still failing, check certificate expiration ssh evelkkbp01.corp.fin openssl x509 -in /etc/kibana/certs/kibana.crt -text -noout | grep -A2 "Validity"

Emergency Procedures

Emergency Stop (Last Resort)

#!/bin/bash echo "⚠️ EMERGENCY STOP INITIATED" ansible all -i inventories/elk-prod.yml \ -m service \ -a "name=elasticsearch state=stopped" \ --become ansible all -i inventories/elk-prod.yml \ -m service \ -a "name=logstash state=stopped" \ --become ansible all -i inventories/elk-prod.yml \ -m service \ -a "name=kibana state=stopped" \ --become echo "All services stopped" echo "Call infrastructure team immediately"

Restore from Snapshot

#!/bin/bash ENDPOINT="https://evelkmnp01.corp.fin:9200" AUTH="-u elastic:$PASSWORD" SNAPSHOT_ID="rhel9-pre-upgrade-20260708" echo "⚠️ RESTORING FROM SNAPSHOT: $SNAPSHOT_ID" # List snapshots curl -s $AUTH "$ENDPOINT/_snapshot/isilon/_all" | jq '.snapshots[] | {name: .snapshot, state: .state}' # Restore curl -X POST "$ENDPOINT/_snapshot/isilon/$SNAPSHOT_ID/_restore" \ $AUTH \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "indices": "*", "include_global_state": true, "partial": false }' # Monitor for i in {1..120}; do STATUS=$(curl -s $AUTH "$ENDPOINT/_snapshot/isilon/$SNAPSHOT_ID/_status" | \ jq '.snapshots[0].state' 2>/dev/null) echo "[$i/120] Status: $STATUS" if [ "$STATUS" = '"SUCCESS"' ]; then echo "✅ Restore complete" break fi sleep 30 done
